title: Establish the basis for Breadth-First Search on Frontier System: XBFS on AMD GPUs
problem: XBFS, a state-of-the-art BFS implementation with adaptive frontier queue generation, performs well on NVIDIA GPUs but encounters challenges when ported to AMD GPUs. The task is to implement XBFS's adaptive strategy on AMD MI250X GPUs in the Frontier supercomputer while achieving competitive performance.
motivation: Frontier is the world's most powerful supercomputer, and efficient BFS implementations are critical for graph analytics workloads in scientific computing.
method: The work adapts XBFS's adaptive strategy that selects different frontier queue generation designs based on BFS level characteristics. Architecture-specific optimizations are developed for AMD MI250X GPUs, leveraging their unique hardware features. The optimized implementation is evaluated on Frontier's AMD GPU architecture.
key_novelty: Adaptation of XBFS's adaptive frontier queue generation strategy specifically for AMD MI250X GPUs with targeted architectural optimizations for the Frontier system.
contributions: Successful port of XBFS to AMD MI250X GPUs with architecture-aware optimizations
Achieves 43 GTEPS per Graphics Compute Die on Frontier
Demonstrates potential to exceed official Frontier Graph500 benchmark performance
Establishes foundation for efficient BFS on AMD-based supercomputing systems
primary_theme: BFS acceleration on AMD MI250X GPUs
